info.title: NodeCraft
info.description:
Central manager API for the NodeCraft game-server hosting platform. It handles authentication, users and quotas, game instances (create/configure/run/backup), per-instance sharing via links, file management (proxied to the workers) and the worker fleet that runs the instances via Docker.

**Authentication:** most routes require a JWT access token (15min) sent in the `accessToken` httpOnly cookie, refreshed through `/auth/refresh`. Some routes are admin only, and the `/worker/*` reporting routes are called by the workers themselves using their API key.

**Authorization:** authentication only proves who you are — each route additionally requires a specific permission (`admin`, `instance:read`, `instance:files:write`, …), stated in the operation description. OpenAPI cannot express these for cookie/API-key schemes, so the lock icon means "needs a token", not "you are allowed". A valid token without the required permission returns `403`.

**Unknown routes:** any path not documented here returns `404` with the standard error body (`error: "NOT_FOUND"`).

**Rate limiting:** the unauthenticated routes (`/auth/login`, `/auth/refresh`, `/auth/reset`, `/auth/forgot`, `/auth/verify`, `POST /user`) are throttled per client IP and answer `429` once the window is exhausted. Failed logins count toward the limit; successful ones do not. Responses carry the standard `RateLimit` headers (`limit`, `remaining`, `reset`).

**Request bodies:** JSON payloads are capped at 100 kB — anything larger is rejected with `413` before the route runs. Malformed JSON returns `400` from the parser, with the parse error in `details`; schema violations return `400` from validation, with one entry per offending field. Every operation that accepts a body can therefore answer `400` or `413` regardless of its own rules.

**Sharing:** every link grants basic instance:read implicitly. Configurable permissions grant additional access. Console history requires instance:console:read, full configuration of every game is readable with instance:read (editing requires instance:edit), roster requires instance:roster:edit, and sharing details require owner/admin access.

**Session revocation:** logout and password reset revoke every previously issued manager access JWT for that account using a database session version. Subsequent authenticated requests return 401, even if the token has not expired. Access JWTs without a version must be renewed through a still-valid refresh cookie or a new login. Worker console access is checked against the current session and permissions every 10 seconds; commands use the latest checked permissions, and revoked read access or token expiry closes the socket on the next check.

cookieAuth.name: accessToken
cookieAuth.description: JWT access token (15min), set as an httpOnly cookie by `POST /auth/login`. The browser sends it automatically on same-origin requests, so "Try it out" works from these docs once you are logged in — there is nothing to paste into Authorize (the cookie is httpOnly and cannot be set from JavaScript).

refreshCookie.name: refreshToken
refreshCookie.description: Opaque refresh token (3 days), stored hashed (SHA-256) in the database and set as an httpOnly cookie scoped to the refresh path. Used only by `POST /auth/refresh` to mint a new access token.

workerApiKey.description: Worker API key sent as `Authorization: Bearer <MANAGER_API_KEY>`, compared against the SHA-256 hash in `worker.apiKey`. Used by the worker→manager reporting routes, not by the frontend.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Login, token refresh/logout, account verification and password reset.

tags.name: User
tags.description: User accounts, profile updates and admin-managed quotas/limits.

tags.name: Instance
tags.description: Game server instances: create, configure, run/stop/restart, backup, console access and ownership/worker placement.

tags.name: Files
tags.description: File manager for an instance's game folder — proxied to the worker that hosts it.

tags.name: Link
tags.description: Shared-access grants that let non-owners use an instance with scoped permissions.

tags.name: Roster
tags.description: Authorized player identities (allow-list / barrier) per instance, resolved to canonical game ids.

tags.name: Worker
tags.description: Worker fleet management and the worker→manager reporting routes (heartbeats, instance status, backup results).

get.description: Public health/info endpoint. Returns basic API metadata (name, version and author). No authentication required. The `docs` field is only present in development — `/docs` is not mounted in production.

summary.example: Central manager API of the NodeCraft platform — create, configure and run game server instances via Docker, with authentication, per-instance permissions, automatic backups and worker fleet monitoring.
